pairs.reason: In 2/3 = 4/6, splitting each third into two equal parts changes the denominator from 3 to 6 without changing the amount represented.
In 2/3 = 4/6, each of the 2 selected thirds becomes 2 sixths, so the numerator becomes 4. Both numerator and denominator are multiplied by 2.
Pictures for 2/3 and 4/6 show equal amounts when their wholes are the same size. Splitting each third in half makes sixths without changing the selected amount.
In 3/5, the denominator says the whole is divided into 5 equal parts; the numerator counts 3 of those parts. Their roles together determine the fraction.
To locate 3/4, divide the interval from 0 to 1 into 4 equal lengths and move 3 of those lengths from 0. The point represents the fraction's value.
With 2 red counters and 3 blue counters, the red-to-blue ratio is 2:3, while the fraction of the whole set that is red is 2/5. The comparison determines the denominator.
A percent is a fraction with denominator 100: 25% = 25/100 = 1/4. Rewriting both forms lets you compare the same portion of a whole.
